description: INDIRECT-driven dynamic references — the TreeCalc surface of OxCalc's CTRO (Calc-Time Rebinding Overlay, W047/W055). Pins calc-time resolution outcomes and the dynamic dependency set (selector + resolved target) including re-binding. `given` supplies the runtime text value of the selector node. OUT OF SCOPE here: the overlay / effective-graph machinery (G_eff, frontier repair) and invalidation timing (engine-internal), and grid/spill expansion/contraction (TreeCalc has no grid — §1). Iterated values for dynamic cycles are governed by §7a (see the cycles theme); exact values are engine/Excel-anchored.

cases.name: static-string INDIRECT parses the string as a tree path
cases.note: Under treecalc-v1 the INDIRECT string is parsed as a tree path; the engine carries it as a runtime-resolved (DynamicResolved) reference even though the string is constant.

cases.name: INDIRECT honors the !-after-sheet alias inside its string
cases.note: The !-after-first-segment allowance is honored inside the parsed string, so "Sheet1!Foo" ≡ the path Sheet1.Foo (§10.3).

cases.name: selector-driven INDIRECT resolves to the named target
cases.note: The dynamic reference depends on BOTH Selector (which picks the path) and the resolved target Branch.A — the CTRO dynamic-target shape.

cases.name: changing the selector re-points the dynamic edge (CTRO rebind)
cases.note: When Selector's text changes to "Branch.B", the Branch.A edge releases and the Branch.B edge activates; the dependency set changes from {Selector, Branch.A} to {Selector, Branch.B}. Downstream dependents (Down = Pick+1) are invalidated and recomputed after the rebind.

cases.name: INDIRECT to a non-existent name fails (no publication)

expect.reason: the string names no node; the dynamic dependency fails (#REF! / DynamicDependencyFailure) and the candidate does not publish — prior published value remains

cases.note: Mirrors OxCalc's local dynamic-reject floor: a diagnostic runtime-effect overlay, DynamicDependencyFailure, no publication bundle.

cases.name: INDIRECT that resolves to its own node is a CTRO self-cycle

expect.engine_ref: DynamicResolved{ via LoopName -> Loop } — candidate-overlay self-cycle

cases.note: The calc-time-resolved edge points the node back at itself; it hits the same no-publication cycle policy as a structural self-cycle. Under the default non-iterative profile this is cycle_blocked; an iterative profile would iterate it (§7a).

cases.name: two INDIRECTs pointing at each other form a CTRO multi-node cycle
cases.note: CycA -> CycB and CycB -> CycA are both calc-time-resolved; the candidate overlay creates a two-node SCC, blocked under the default profile (§7a).

cases.name: a dynamic cycle becomes acyclic when the selector changes (release/re-entry)
cases.note: When LoopName changes from "Loop" to "Branch.A", the prior self-cycle is released; the reference re-points to an acyclic target, the node re-enters calculation and publishes, and downstream dependents recompute. Mirrors OxCalc's CTRO cycle-release/re-entry scenario.
